main_body: A flat cobblestone-style ground patch (steampunk floor), a seamless repeating pattern of dark grey-brown stones with lighter highlights.
top_band: none (terrain texture, no standing body; column scan shows repeating stone-course bands of 1-3 rows)
evidence: The candidate is a terrain tile pattern, not a standing object. It has no top/front structure to judge, and the 3/4 contract does not apply to flat ground. It reads as a uniformly repeating floor texture with no vertical faces, so no 3/4 failure modes are present.

style.evidence: The candidate uses 5 distinct colours in a neutral grey-brown ramp, with a 100% near-neutral dark edge share, so the outline is near-black rather than a tinted material tone. The pattern is a tightly repeating cobble scallop with no 5x5 flat areas (0%), so it is not flat. Against the paving reference, though, it is on par: 5 colours per tile vs 7, with 5 vs 7 distinct colours total, and the paving reference also has 80% neutral dark edges. It falls well short of the grass reference (26 per tile, 80 colours), but that is a different material. The cobble is very regular and mechanical, with the same highlight repeated at identical positions, which looks like a stamped tile rather than hand-shaded stones. The colour count is slightly below the paving reference, and the neutral dark lines add a mild sticker look. Overall it is a slightly lower density than the same-kind reference and does not match it for craft.
